## Project Overview

Mocha is an open-source, general-purpose JavaScript testing framework that prioritizes flexibility, stability, and compatibility. [PROJECT_CHARTER.md:9-12] The package supports both Node.js and browser usage, and is described as a test framework for Node.js and the browser. [package.json]

The main implementation is JavaScript, with CommonJS, ESM, and browser-specific modules visible under `lib/`. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/browser/highlight-tags.js:32-37][lib/nodejs/esm-utils.cjs:158-172] TypeScript is used for type declarations and type checking. [lib/types.d.ts:19-22][tsconfig.json] The repository also uses Rollup for the browser bundle, Playwright for browser tests, ESLint and Prettier for code quality, and Astro Starlight for the documentation site. [AGENTS.md:37-42][package.json][docs/README.md:1-6]

Likely runtime entry points include the command-line launcher `bin/mocha.js`, the main Mocha implementation in `lib/mocha.cjs`, and the browser entry module `browser-entry.js`. [bin/mocha.js:41-46][lib/mocha.cjs:168-173][browser-entry.js:90-100] The documentation site is a separate application under `docs/`. [docs/README.md:1-6]

## Setup / Installation

Use Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`; Node.js 22 LTS is recommended. [AGENTS.md:22-27] npm is the supported package manager; the repository explicitly says not to use pnpm or yarn. [AGENTS.md:22-27] Google Chrome is required when running browser tests locally. [AGENTS.md:22-27]

From the repository root, install dependencies with:

```sh
npm install
```

[AGENTS.md:43-53] For a clean CI-style installation, use `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; the workflows use this form. [AGENTS.md:47-53][.github/workflows/npm-script.yml] Optional dependency installation failures can be ignored unless you are building the documentation, and `npm install --ignore-scripts` is offered as an alternative. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]

Documentation work uses a separate package and dependency installation step. [AGENTS.md:142-150] The documented setup is:

```sh
cd docs
npm i
npm run generate
```

[docs/README.md:7-17] The repository evidence does not specify any required local environment variables; the setup instructions only document Node.js, npm, Chrome, and dependency installation. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-19]

## Running Locally

Run the repository's main validation workflow with:

```sh
npm test
```

This runs the repository's code validations, including linting and tests in Node.js and browsers. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-33] The supplied `package.json` evidence does not show a standalone application development server or a local port for the core project. [package.json]

Build the generated browser bundle with:

```sh
npm run clean
npm run build
```

The build uses Rollup, and `npm run clean` removes `mocha.js` and `mocha.js.map`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][package.json] Do not edit those generated bundle files directly. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][AGENTS.md:37-42]

For focused development, the documented watch command is:

```sh
npx mocha --watch test/unit/
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:34-49] Mocha’s watch implementation monitors configured paths and schedules another run when matching files change. [lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:444-500] It also supports restarting the current watch run by entering `rs`. [docs/src/content/docs/running/cli.mdx:482-489][lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:537-542]

The documentation site has its own local development command:

```sh
cd docs
npm i
npm run generate
npm run dev
```

[docs/README.md:7-17] The docs package uses Astro for both development and preview commands. [docs/package.json]

## Project Structure

- `bin/` contains the command-line launcher; `bin/mocha.js` is a likely executable entry point. [bin/mocha.js:41-46]
- `lib/` contains the main runtime implementation, including the Mocha class, CLI processing, runners, suites, tests, reporters, plugins, Node.js helpers, browser helpers, and type declarations. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/cli/cli.js:80-97][lib/runner.js:1195-1224][lib/suite.js:417-445][lib/test.js:17-30][lib/types.d.ts:19-22]
- `lib/cli/` implements command parsing, configuration lookup, file discovery, run orchestration, and watch mode. [lib/cli/config.cjs:17-26][lib/cli/lookup-files.js:106-117][lib/cli/run-helpers.cjs:159-206][lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:444-500]
- `lib/nodejs/` contains Node.js-specific worker, ESM, serialization, and parallel execution modules. [lib/nodejs/buffered-worker-pool.cjs:85-93][lib/nodejs/esm-utils.cjs:158-172][lib/nodejs/parallel-buffered-runner.cjs:410-412]
- `lib/reporters/` contains built-in reporters such as HTML, JSON, JSON stream, TAP, and XUnit. [lib/reporters/html.js:58-88][lib/reporters/json.js:108-123][lib/reporters/json-stream.js:66-87][lib/reporters/tap.js:150-185][lib/reporters/xunit.js:140-148]
- `test/` contains smoke, unit, integration, interface, reporter, browser, compiler, plugin, and parallel-mode tests. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]
- `docs/` is a separate Astro Starlight documentation application with content under `docs/src/content/docs/`. [docs/README.md:1-6][docs/src/content/docs/getting-started.mdx:1-7]
- `example/config/` contains illustrative Node.js configuration examples rather than project boilerplates. [example/config/README.md:1-7]
- `repro/` is an optional, separate minimal Node.js project for reproducing end-user behavior against the repository. [repro/README.md:1-9][repro/README.md:12-35]

## Testing

The repository uses Mocha itself as its test framework, with test files written using interfaces such as BDD and QUnit. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/interfaces/qunit.spec.js:3-5] Tests use assertion and test utility dependencies including Chai, Sinon, Unexpected, and related packages. [package.json]

Run the full validation suite with:

```sh
npm test
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-33] Targeted commands include smoke tests, Node.js unit tests, integration tests, interface tests, reporter tests, browser tests, TypeScript checking, and linting. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:34-49] The repository’s Node.js test scripts invoke `node bin/mocha.js` and use NYC for coverage in several test paths. [package.json]

Important focused commands include:

```sh
npm run test-smoke
npm run test-node:unit
npm run test-node:integration
npm run test-node:interfaces
npm run test-node:reporters
npm run test-browser
npm run tsc
npm run lint
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:34-49] Browser testing uses Playwright and the `test-browser` script cleans and builds the bundle before running the browser tests. [package.json][AGENTS.md:87-92] Google Chrome is required for local browser testing. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]

The main test locations are `test/smoke/`, `test/unit/`, `test/integration/`, `test/interfaces/`, `test/reporters/`, and `test/browser-specific/`. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9] Integration tests also use fixture files under `test/integration/fixtures/`. [test/integration/fixtures/__default__.fixture.js:5-9][test/integration/fixtures/passing-sync.fixture.js:3-6]

Tests commonly use `describe`, `it`, `beforeEach`, and `afterEach`, with synchronous, callback-based asynchronous, Promise-based, skipped, retried, and parallel test cases represented in the fixtures. [test/integration/fixtures/__default__.fixture.js:5-9][test/integration/fixtures/passing-async.fixture.js:4-6][test/integration/fixtures/pending/skip-sync-beforeEach.fixture.cjs:6-13][test/integration/fixtures/options/parallel/test-a.fixture.js:1-3] Sinon cleanup is commonly performed in `afterEach` hooks. [test/node-unit/buffered-worker-pool.spec.cjs:48-50][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52]

The supplied evidence identifies test directories and recurring setup patterns, but does not identify a single global test setup file. [test/integration/helpers.cjs:347-349][test/reporters/helpers.cjs:226-229]
